llm.summary: This is a documentation-only skill for using CellCog, with optional file upload and connected-tool features that are disclosed and user-triggered.

dimensions.detail: The skill can involve uploading local files and using real browser profiles or connected SaaS tools, which is proportionate to its stated purpose but should be used with deliberate scoping.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation guidance is limited to installing the CellCog Python SDK with pip and setting CELLCOG_API_KEY; the skill artifact itself contains no executable scripts.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions are broad and promotional, but the sensitive actions described require explicit prompt tags or SDK flags; there is no artifact evidence of hidden execution or automatic delegation.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Notify mode uses a background daemon/WebSocket and CellCog chats can continue after timeout, but this behavior is documented and tied to task completion rather than hidden persistence.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill’s broad multimodal sub-agent purpose matches its documented capabilities: creating CellCog chats, uploading explicitly tagged files, generating outputs, and optionally enabling browser or SaaS-tool integrations.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you intend to use CellCog as an external AI service. Only wrap files in SHOW_FILE tags when you are willing to upload them, avoid secrets and private keys, and enable browser or Gmail/Notion-style tools only for accounts and scopes you are comfortable sharing with CellCog.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: The universal sub-agent framing is broad, but it is coherent with the product’s stated purpose and the artifact does not instruct automatic use for sensitive tasks.
[SQP-2] expected: Browser and SaaS-tool access are sensitive, but the artifact presents them as optional enable_browse/enable_tools settings with tool selection; stronger privacy guidance would help, but the evidence does not show hidden or automatic account access.
